rv.q: Add in Fisher, now a sought-after Broadway actress and a performer with a warm-centered and highly skilled wrangler of people and feelings, and you have an uncommonly special evening.
“Every Brilliant Thing” is an uplifting show about gratitude, played at just the right emotional register.
This is one of those plays destined to remain with me for a very long time.
“Every Brilliant Thing,” a solo play by Duncan MacMillan in a masterful revival at Writers Theatre.
I can’t imagine a better time to stage this play.
Director Kimberly Senior has guided Fisher to a remarkable performance that is deceivingly natural and immensely convincing.
Every Brilliant Thing is a theatrical surprise.
Brilliant’s list eventually tops a million entries, and this production earns equally joyful praises.

Fisher’s beguiling performance—aided by audience volunteers who stand in for the narrator’s dad, school therapist, college lit professor, and spouse—creates a room for us to collectively think about what lights our way when it feels like the entire world is blinding us.
It's a great reminder of all the reasons for living we take for granted, and the play does a nice job of driving that home.
Directed by Kimberly Senior, Fisher is brilliant and so is the play.
You’ll leave this joyous, life-affirming play feeling hopeful and inspired.
This creatively inspired and nicely accomplished show navigates between joyfulness and sadness, often at the same moment.

cn.t: Fisher delivers a virtuoso, emotionally engaging performance in this cleverly structured one-hander about depression and gratitude. Critics praise the interactive format and poignant balance of humor and heartbreak.
